artifacts.summary: Full re-grep inventory of hand-rolled specs/state.json writers surviving the skill-skeleton collapse: 29 SKILL.md files / 69 sites within the declared skills/ file_scope (founder 15/37, present 5/17, lean 4/10, cslib 5/5, web and epidemiology-skills already clean); flags a scope-boundary gap (16 commands/*.md files / 22 sites outside the declared file_scope but inside the task's own FULL-source-store WORK item), a cross-repo hardcoded-path bug in skill-pr-implementation, two schema-conformance risks (base_branch, forcing_data), and recommends a new generalized lint plus the conversion pattern to copy from already-converted core/web skills.

memory_candidates.content: When re-grepping a source store for hand-rolled specs/state.json writers (the jq-to-shared-temp-then-mv anti-pattern state-write.sh replaces), check three temp-path variants, not just one: 'specs/tmp/state.json' (most common), 'specs/state.json.tmp' (a single-file variant), and '/tmp/state.tmp' or a hardcoded absolute path via a shell variable (machine-global or cross-repo, the worst variant since it can point outside the current repo entirely). A grep anchored only on the first variant will silently miss the other two.

A task's declared file_scope in state.json can be narrower than what the task description's own WORK items/VERIFICATION BAR text actually require (e.g. file_scope names only skills/ subdirectories while WORK item 1 says 're-grep the FULL source store'). When this mismatch is found during research, do not silently pick one interpretation -- report both inventories (in-scope vs. full-source-store) separately and let planning make the explicit call, mirroring how a prior conversion task (state-write.sh archive/vault coverage) declared and justified its own scoped-grep exclusion list rather than claiming an unqualified 'zero hits'.

state-schema.json's projectEntry sets additionalProperties: false. Any extension skill/command that writes a non-enumerated field onto an active_projects[] entry (observed: base_branch from cslib PR skills, forcing_data from founder task-creation commands) will fail a future validate-state.sh --deep / hard schema gate even after its writer mechanism is correctly converted to state-write.sh, because state-write.sh validates JSON well-formedness only, not schema conformance. Converting the mechanism and fixing schema conformance are two separate concerns that are easy to conflate.
